speaker: georgedaskalopou
text: Yes. I've got four points to make, and in a summary, I assume it's not going to take too long. I refer to the Council report of the original development application plans, which was critical on a number of points. It was stated that the development control panel in a heritage area required a pitch roof with eaves in keeping with those of the heritage area. The pitch roof was requested by the adjoining neighbours and 12 of the local residents who'd made submissions. The roof of the amended plans does not achieve this, and in the Council's report of the amended plans, there is no specific reason given as to why this requirement of the development control plan has not been followed. My second point is the height of the north section of the proposed building is over six metres. The height limit is six metres. This exceeds the development control plan height. No reason, again, has been given as to why this is deemed compliant. My third point, in my submission to the amended plans, I have noted that my main outdoor living area is where I spend considerable time. This is at the north side of the building, facing the Lane Cove River. The proposed building, which will now extend beyond my building line to the north, this will result in shadowing of my veranda and outdoor living area in the afternoon and significantly diminish my amenities related to my outdoor living. This will also have the effect of diminishing the view of the heritage building as seen from the Lane Cove River. This effect is due to the first floor level being extended in the northerly direction as compared to the current building and beyond the northern boundary of my building. As a heritage building, I do not have options of moving my building line to make any adjustments. I am sure the panel also knows of the extra costs of maintaining a heritage building. My fourth point is, I note that the outhouse along the common boundary wall is still listed in the amended plans. This is a change room and showers for the pool. There is currently no such building and this is not necessary as this can be provided within the proposed building as it currently is in the existing building. It is listed as a non-compliance and should be withdrawn. I note the reason for this, for its maintenance is that it is below the fence level. However, this does not address the reason for request of withdrawal, which is because of the resulting noise levels directly adjacent to our outdoor living area. So, I'd like to summarise now. At the recent site visit meeting by the local planning group, I expressed that our main concern was the effect of the proposed building on our main outdoor living area and our northern veranda. We requested a setback of the proposed first floor area such that we could maintain our amenities. It is my request that this approval is postponed until the matter listed above, the matters I've listed above can be resolved. I am happy to answer any questions from the panel. I would also like to request if there is any appeal process which is available to address these matters. I think that covers what my concerns are. Thank you.
